name: Mission context
purpose: A-to-B service crosses the relay aircraft. Carrier command/status is a separate path; terrain constrains the service geometry.

name: Service requirements
purpose: Engineering requirements derive from the service need. Dashed verify links identify check responsibilities; they do not claim demonstrated communications performance.

name: Recovery requirements
purpose: Energy, installed mass and continuous demand constrain the planned sortie. Thresholds remain illustrative and actual recovery has not been demonstrated.

name: Interface and evidence requirements
purpose: Installation evidence, comparison records and reproducibility have different checks. The interface review remains open even when the numerical tests pass.

name: Operational use cases
purpose: Rounded nodes represent use cases. Actor associations express participation, not execution order. Restore readiness is described but not simulated.

name: Mission functions
purpose: Solid arrows indicate the nominal function sequence. Dashed arrows indicate supporting responsibilities, avoiding the suggestion that monitoring and power are extra timed flight segments.

name: Logical blocks
purpose: Composition groups responsibilities independently of hardware. Class compartments list responsibilities, not implemented software methods.

name: Physical composition
purpose: Composition shows owned physical groups. Each box is a reusable block type; the labeled relationship is the part role. Both battery choices use this same structure.

name: Airborne interfaces
purpose: Solid edges carry electrical supply; the dashed edge carries flight commands. Interface types and conjugated port directions remain explicit in the model tables.

name: Service and carrier interfaces
purpose: The served endpoints are external. Mission traffic and carrier control enter different aircraft responsibilities; no throughput or command-link reliability is demonstrated here.

name: Mission lifecycle
purpose: The diagram specifies intended operational decisions. The evaluator checks a planned sortie and does not implement live flight control or off-nominal recovery.

name: Installed mass constraint
purpose: Undirected lines mean equality bindings between named values and constraint parameters. The mount increment is separate from pack mass. Python evaluates the relation.

name: Energy and reserve constraint
purpose: One reserve deduction is applied to usable energy. Binding lines state equality, not calculation order; the constraint expression is listed below the figure in the book.

name: Supported dwell constraint
purpose: The maximum energy-supported dwell retains its sign. A negative value means the nonservice sortie already exceeds the allowance. Radio, mass and power checks still apply.

name: Configuration decision
purpose: Six options share one mission and requirement basis. The selection is provisional and never converts missing hardware or physical evidence into a pass.

name: Propulsion power constraint
purpose: Fixed rotor geometry and a propulsion-only reference operating point define the provisional hover electrical law. The shared multiplier is a sensitivity input, not a wind model.

name: Segment energy constraint
purpose: Propulsion and auxiliary loads are accounted at the main bus. The payload regulator loss enters once. Duration times power is converted from joules to Wh by dividing by 3600.
